keyframe_review.note: Years, Amami and Miyako. Cliopatria's 2,617 km2 is the 1429 outline plus about one cell to the south-west (bbox west edge 125.2 E, 24.7 N: Miyako), dated 1497. The Ryukyu Kingdom page dates no earlier Miyako event: its timeline reads '1500: Sakishima Islands annexed by Ryukyu', its intro says the kingdom 'subsequently extended the kingdom to the Amami Islands and Sakishima Islands', and Miyako is otherwise named only for an 1874 monument. The Sakishima Islands page says they 'include the Miyako Islands and the Yaeyama Islands', so the 1500 annexation covers Miyako as well as Yaeyama; the Miyako cell is therefore taken out of 1497-1499 and added in 1500 (see ryukyu-kingdom_1500 and the 1500 gain). The same page has a Miyako chief who 'paid tribute to Satto, the king of the Chūzan kingdom' (undated within Satto's reign 1350-1397; 1365 is when he 'unified Miyako'): a tributary link, not the annexation the Ryukyu page dates to 1500. The infobox gives no area, so no ratio.

ledger.note: 1609: the Ryukyu Kingdom becomes a vassal of the Satsuma Domain. Infobox 'Vassal state of the Satsuma Domain (1609–1872)'; 'The Ryukyu Kingdom became a vassal state of the Satsuma Domain of Japan after the invasion of Ryukyu in 1609'; the timeline dates the kings' vassalage to 1611 ('Kings of Ryukyu become vassals to the daimyō of the Satsuma Domain'), with the peace treaty and the annexation of the Amami and Tokara Islands. The year is the infobox's; month 5 is the fall of Shuri (Invasion of Ryukyu page: 'on May 5, some Satsuma officers entered the castle'), and the surrender documents follow in 1611. The Amami Islands pass to Satsuma outright in 1611 (the loss below), so the vassal land is Okinawa, Miyako and Yaeyama. Counterpart is satsuma-domain, the party the infobox names; it has no dossier yet, and tokugawa-shogunate is the alternative if the group treats the han as internal units (the dates would not change). The kingdom stayed a Ming and then Qing tributary at the same time (the Invasion page's 'dual subordination').

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-b on 2026-10-18 from two pages (the budget of 1-2).

Cliopatria stops: the Ryukyu Kingdom row covers 1429-1520 only, but the kingdom lasted to 1872 and the Ryukyu Domain to 1879. The dossier therefore runs to 1879 and adds new keyframes for 1447 (Amami), 1500 (Yaeyama) and 1611-1879 (without Amami). The three Cliopatria shapes are all kept as the base outline (Okinawa Island, plus a Miyako cell from 1497) with 'adjust' verdicts.

Unsettled: (1) Miyako, Kume and Kerama: the page gives no submission date for Miyako; the 1497 Cliopatria shape includes it; unverified. (2) Amami: the page has 1447 for Amami Ōshima (Shō Shitatsu), 1466 for two attacks on Kikai, 'rebellions in the Amami region' put down in 1537; the other northern islands are undated, so the whole group is drawn from 1447 at confidence 2. (3) Tokara: the Ryukyu Kingdom timeline says Satsuma annexed 'the Amami and Tokara Islands' in 1611; the Invasion page says nothing of Tokara; only the Amami part is drawn. (4) Dates on the Ryukyu page that disagree: Shō Shin's reign 1477 (table) or 1478 (text); annexation 27 March 1879 (text) or 4 April 1879 (infobox); the Satsuma invasion 5 April 1609 (infobox) against the day-by-day account (Amami 7 April, Shuri 5 May). (5) The kingdom's 1429-1644 Ming, 1644-1646 Southern Ming and 1646-1872 Qing tributary status and Satsuma's vassal status 1609-1872 (infobox) are suzerain-side events for the Ming, Qing and Satsuma dossiers; the Japanese order to end tribute came in 1875. No ruler strip is given because the page's king table was not read in full.

Needs dossiers: satsuma-domain (the Edo-period Satsuma han; counterpart of the 1609 contest, the 1611 loss and the 1609-1872 vassalage). Gazetteer names missing: 'Amami Islands' and 'Yaeyama Islands' (regions; Amami Ōshima, Kikai, Tokunoshima, Okinoerabu, Yoron, about 27-28.5 N 128-130 E; Ishigaki, Iriomote, Yonaguni, about 24-24.5 N 123-124.5 E).

Handover to the Chūzan dossier: Chūzan's last drawn year is 1428; this dossier draws 1429. The grid cells are about 253 km2, so the Okinawa shapes are six or seven cells.
